title: に / へ — direction and destination (“to ～”)
summary: After a place noun, に and へ show the destination of a movement verb such as 行く, 来る, 帰る. へ is read ‘e’. In this use the two are almost interchangeable. They attach to a noun.

patterns.gloss: place + に/へ + verb of movement (行く・来る・帰る)

body.p: Put に or へ after the place you are heading to: 学校へ行きます, 駅に行きます. The meaning is the same, ‘go to the school / station’.
へ stresses the direction you move toward, while に stresses the point you arrive at. In everyday speech you can use either. With 帰る (return) and 着く (arrive), に is very common.
As a particle, へ is pronounced ‘e’, not ‘he’: 学校へ is gakkō e. It is still written with へ.

examples.ja: 学校（がっこう）へ行（い）きます。

examples.note: 駅に行きます is also correct.
With 帰る, に is very natural.

pitfalls: Don't pronounce the particle へ as ‘he’; it is ‘e’.
に has other jobs too (time, place of existence). Here it only marks a destination after a movement verb.
